claims.paraphrase: For a supported noncredit decline, OCC reverses the credit allowance on HFS transfer, uses a separate valuation allowance, and reverses that valuation allowance on return to HFI before reassessing credit losses.
claims.exclusions: Use a new multi-loan ledger with a stipulated, objectively supported interest-rate-only decline. Exclude credit-driven regulatory charge-offs, mortgage loans, origination, sale recognition, interest accrual, fees, taxes and source examples. Include a separately stipulated return-to-hold decision.

claims.paraphrase: For a probable, reasonably estimable loss, OCC uses the better estimate within a range or its minimum when no point is better.
claims.exclusions: Use fictional independent matters with supplied probable-loss and reasonable-estimate conclusions, a best estimate or no better point, later updated estimates and settlement cash. Exclude appeals, court judgments, legal advice, gain/insurance contingencies, discounting, tax and source scenarios.

claims.paraphrase: OCC keeps equipment classified as held for use while still used and shortens its depreciation horizon to reach residual value when use ends.
claims.exclusions: Use a new three-asset service-retirement schedule with stipulated straight-line policy, residual values and an independently supplied conclusion that no separate impairment adjustment is required. Exclude outsourcing contract terms, sale, held-for-sale classification, leases, software, impairment measurement, tax and source examples.

claims.paraphrase: OCC puts costs directly related to a successful stock offering against offering proceeds in equity; unsuccessful-offering costs affect current expense.
claims.exclusions: Use a fictional offering register with supplied cost-eligibility conclusions, two independently completed common-stock issues and a separately abandoned proposal. Exclude deferred interim cost policy, debt/convertible instruments, mixed securities, warrants, employee awards, SEC registrant-specific rules, tax and source examples.
